info.title: FilesHub API
info.summary: Zero-cost file storage, email sending, and developer utilities over HTTP.
info.description:
FilesHub is a file-storage and developer-utility API. Upload files and get a stable public URL, send transactional email from verified domains, run background jobs, and call 40+ utility groups — all authenticated with a per-project X-API-Key header. This spec covers the core integration surface (objects, emails, templates, schedules, jobs, version/health) plus the whole Public Management plane. The full list of stateless developer utilities is summarized at https://fileshub-docs.zaions.com/api/utilities-index. Docs: https://fileshub-docs.zaions.com.

TWO PLANES, TWO ENVELOPES — do not reuse one parser for both. The v1 data plane answers {"success", "data"} on email, a FLAT body on POST /objects, and a bare {"message"} on error. The Management plane (/api/public/v1, the `Management API` tag) answers {"data"} on success and {"error": {code, message, details?}} on failure, and never carries `success`.

HOW THIS SPEC IS MAINTAINED: it is written by hand — nothing generates it from the Laravel routes — so where it and the running API disagree, THE API IS RIGHT. Verified against the live routes and controllers on 2026-08-04 at backend_version 2026.08.01.2, covering all 33 Management routes. Report a divergence rather than coding around it.

On a 403 TOKEN_PERMISSION_DENIED, all four gates report details.required_scope as the access token’s own column name (`can_read_vault`, `can_reveal_vault`, `can_manage_supabase`, `can_read_supabase_tokens`) — live since `2026.08.04.1`, deployed 2026-08-04. Releases before it returned two shorter labels on the Supabase gates (`supabase_projects` / `supabase_tokens`) that matched no column; the enum below accepts all six, so either release works.

Since 2026.08.19.1 the response reports all six counts and the call is audited as public_api.project.deleted with those counts in its metadata; before that release `cascade` named only api_keys and stored_objects, so the credentials went unmentioned, and the call left no audit row at all.

post.description: Add an allowed origin. Domains are validated against the scheme+port policy and stored canonically (example.com -> https://example.com). Browser extensions use type=domain with an extension scheme, where the host is the extension id: chrome-extension://<id> (also moz-extension://, safari-web-extension://), no port and no wildcard. Origins configured platform-wide by an administrator (global origins) also apply to every restricted key and are not listed here — read them with GET /global-origins and test candidates with POST /global-origins/check before adding, so you do not create a duplicate the key never needed.

get.description: Every ACTIVE origin an administrator has registered platform-wide. Each is accepted by every restricted API key in addition to that key's own origins, and never appears in a key's own origin list. Read-only and open to any valid access token; global origins are created and edited only in the dashboard, because a rule that affects every project is an operator decision. Check these before adding an origin to a key, so you do not create a duplicate the key never needed.

post.summary: Check whether origins are already covered globally
post.description: Ask whether specific origins are already allowed platform-wide, then add only the ones reporting covered=false. Use this instead of comparing the list yourself: matching is not string equality. A wildcard rule https://*.example.com covers its subdomains AND the bare apex, an apex rule https://example.com covers no subdomain at all, and http://localhost:* covers every port. This endpoint runs the same matcher request-time enforcement uses, so its answer cannot disagree with it. Up to 50 candidates per request; verdicts return one per candidate in request order. A value that can never be a legal origin is a verdict (200 with covered=false and a reason), not a request-level error, so one bad candidate does not discard the answers for the rest.

200.description: One verdict per candidate, in request order

value.description: The origin to test. A domain may be written bare (example.com); it is canonicalized before matching.

cert_fingerprint.description: Android only: the signing fingerprint the app sends as X-Android-Cert (colons optional). A global rule that pins certificates cannot report covered without it.

get.description: Every service and field the project vault can hold: label, where to find the value, whether it is secret, whether it may ship in a browser bundle, and its .env name. Identical for every project — it describes the SHAPE of the vault, never its contents — so ANY VALID TOKEN MAY READ IT: this endpoint needs neither can_read_vault nor any other scope, and cannot 403. Currently 18 services and 87 fields. Read it before guessing a field name.
Projects this token can see, each with its identifiers and which services are configured. Requires `can_read_vault`. Paginated: default 20, max 50.

post.description: Many services, and optionally the whole link list, in ONE transaction — the call a seeding run uses. Every service and field is validated BEFORE the transaction opens, so an invalid entry anywhere means nothing at all is written. `links` is a full replace when present and untouched when absent. Requires `can_write_vault` (default false; it implies `can_read_vault` but NOT `can_reveal_vault`). A missing scope is 403 `TOKEN_PERMISSION_DENIED` with `details.required_scope`; an out-of-scope project is 404. Added in backend 2026.08.20.1 — the vault was read-only before that.

put.description: Partial upsert. An **absent** key leaves that field untouched; an explicit **null** deletes its row. For a registry-declared field the registry decides whether the value is secret — a caller-supplied `secrets` flag is honoured only on the freeform `general` service, where it defaults to true. A `file`-typed field is refused here (422 VAULT_FIELD_IS_A_FILE); use the vault-files endpoint. Linked (`supabase`) and derived (`fileshub`) services refuse writes entirely. Requires `can_write_vault` (default false; it implies `can_read_vault` but NOT `can_reveal_vault`). A missing scope is 403 `TOKEN_PERMISSION_DENIED` with `details.required_scope`; an out-of-scope project is 404. Added in backend 2026.08.20.1 — the vault was read-only before that.

get.description: The real bytes of a stored file — google-services.json, a plist, a service-account JSON, an Android keystore — with its original filename and an `X-Checksum-Sha256` header. Requires `can_reveal_vault`. A file that is stored but cannot be decrypted returns 409 PLAINTEXT_UNAVAILABLE with `details.reason: "undecryptable"`, which is a different answer from missing.

parameters.description: `service.key`, e.g. `firebase.google_services_json` — the identifier a reveal returns in each file's `download`.

X-Checksum-Sha256.description: sha256 of the plaintext bytes, so a caller can verify what it wrote to disk.

Content-Type.description: The file's stored mime type, or application/octet-stream when none was recorded.

Content-Disposition.description: attachment with the original filename — curl -OJ writes it under the right name.

post.description: Accepts either a multipart `file` part or a JSON `{filename, content_base64}` body. The size cap (FILESHUB_VAULT_MAX_FILE_KB, default 1024 KB) applies to the DECODED bytes in both cases, and base64 is decoded strictly — a corrupted payload is refused rather than stored as something that fails later. Requires `can_write_vault` (default false; it implies `can_read_vault` but NOT `can_reveal_vault`). A missing scope is 403 `TOKEN_PERMISSION_DENIED` with `details.required_scope`; an out-of-scope project is 404. Added in backend 2026.08.20.1 — the vault was read-only before that.

post.summary: Retire an orphaned service onto declared fields
post.description: Moves every row from one service to another, renaming keys as it goes. `from` MAY be a service the registry never declared — that is the purpose; `to` may not. The move is validated whole before anything is written, so an undeclared destination field means nothing moves. A key with no entry in `keys` is carried over unchanged and validated like any other. A source row that cannot be decrypted answers 409 PLAINTEXT_UNAVAILABLE rather than moving a null over a good value.\n\nThe path is `vault-move`, not `vault/move`, because a literal beside the parameterised `vault/{service}` would be an ambiguous path template — and keeping the free-text source service in the body avoids URL-encoding a name that may contain spaces. Requires `can_write_vault` (default false; it implies `can_read_vault` but NOT `can_reveal_vault`). A missing scope is 403 `TOKEN_PERMISSION_DENIED` with `details.required_scope`; an out-of-scope project is 404. Added in backend 2026.08.20.1 — the vault was read-only before that.

ApiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyHeader.description: Per-project API key. Send on every authenticated request.

AppId.name: X-App-Id
AppId.description: Required only for app-restricted keys: the Android package or iOS bundle id (X-Android-Package is an accepted alias).

AndroidCert.name: X-Android-Cert
AndroidCert.description: Android signing-cert fingerprint (SHA-256 or SHA-1). Required when the key's android origin pins certificate fingerprints. See https://fileshub-docs.zaions.com/getting-started/api-key-restrictions.

Forbidden.description: Key lacks the required scope, or origin/app not allowed.

PaginationMeta.description: Pagination state for every list endpoint. Default page size is 20 and the hard maximum is 50; a larger `per_page` is CLAMPED to 50, never rejected, and `message` says so. Offset-based on purpose: a page number and a total cannot be expressed by cursor pagination.

per_page.description: Rows in this page, after clamping to max_per_page.

total.description: Total rows matching the query across all pages.

last_page.description: Number of the final page; equals current_page on the last one.

from.description: 1-based index of the first row in this page; null when empty.

to.description: 1-based index of the last row in this page; null when empty.

count.description: Rows actually returned in this response.

has_more.description: True when further pages exist. Equivalent to next_page != null.

remaining_items.description: Rows after this page. Zero on the last page.

remaining_pages.description: Pages after this one. Zero on the last page.

next_page.description: Send this as ?page= to continue; null on the last page.

prev_page.description: Previous page number; null on the first page.

max_per_page.description: Hard ceiling for per_page (50). A larger request is clamped.

default_per_page.description: Page size used when per_page is omitted (20).

mime_type.description: Server-detected MIME type, sniffed from the file's contents. Any Content-Type declared on the uploaded multipart part is ignored, and this is also the type the object is served with. Treat as authoritative — there is no field to override it.

domain.description: Verified sending domain. Omitted => admin default with fallback.

scheduled_at.description: Send once at a future time.

slug.description: Immutable once set; auto-generated from name if omitted.

EmailTemplateUpdate.description: Any subset of the create fields except slug (immutable).

ManagementError.description: The Management plane's only error envelope. Note it differs from the v1 data plane, which answers with a bare {"message": "..."} and no code.

code.description: Machine-readable code. Branch on this, never on the message text.

details.description: Present only on the codes that carry one; the key is ABSENT otherwise, never null. TOKEN_PERMISSION_DENIED carries `required_scope`; PLAINTEXT_UNAVAILABLE carries `reason` ("undecryptable" | "not_retained"); VALIDATION_FAILED carries per-field message arrays.

required_scope.description: The token flag the caller is missing — the access token's own column name, so the 403 names the switch to enable in Nova: `can_read_vault`, `can_reveal_vault`, `can_manage_supabase`, `can_read_supabase_tokens`. Live since `2026.08.04.1` (deployed 2026-08-04). Releases before it answered two shorter forms on the Supabase gates (`supabase_projects`, `supabase_tokens`) that matched no column; the enum keeps all six so a client works against either release.

reason.description: On PLAINTEXT_UNAVAILABLE: `undecryptable` means a value IS stored but was encrypted under a different APP_KEY (re-enter it); `not_retained` means nothing was ever stored (rotate instead). The remedy differs, which is why the two are distinguished.

ProjectPublic.description: A project on the Management plane. Credential VALUES are never part of this shape — those live behind the project vault's own scopes. Note `repo_url` / `repo_is_public` are flat here, while the vault views nest the same two as `repo: { url, is_public }`.

public_id.description: ULID. Accepted wherever {project} appears, alongside the numeric id and the slug.

app_identifier.description: Reverse-DNS app id. IMMUTABLE once published to a store.

platforms.description: Always an array; empty rather than null when unset.

tech_stack.description: Always an array; empty rather than null when unset.

supabase_project_id.description: The registered Supabase project this app uses, or null. Readable without any vault scope — it is a pointer, not a credential. WRITABLE on POST /projects and PATCH /projects/{project} since 2026.08.19.1, which needs can_manage_supabase and refuses a target the token could not already see (linking widens what the token may read). Record it once instead of re-deriving it every session.

api_keys_count.description: Keys in this project, including inactive and rotated-away ones.

ProjectListItem.description: A row from GET /projects — the project plus its key count.

api_keys.description: Abbreviated key list, newest first. Deliberately narrower than ApiKeySafe — for the full representation call the api-keys endpoints.

ProjectWithApiKeys.description: The response of GET /projects/{project} — the project plus an abbreviated api_keys list.

ApiKeySafe.description: API key without the hash or plaintext.

allow_no_origin.description: Restricted keys only: allow requests that send no Origin and no X-App-Id (server/CLI/native consumers).

value.description: Canonical origin for domains (scheme://host[:port]); package/bundle id for android/ios.

GlobalOriginPublic.description: An origin every restricted API key accepts, platform-wide. Only active rules are ever returned, so there is no is_active field.

value.description: Canonical origin for domains (scheme://host[:port], possibly with a *. host wildcard or a :* port wildcard); package/bundle id for android/ios.

note.description: The administrator's reason this origin is trusted for every key.

GlobalOriginCheckResult.description: One candidate's verdict. Add the candidate to a key only when covered is false.

canonical_value.description: The canonical form the candidate was matched on — the exact origin a browser sends, and the exact string POST .../origins would store. Null for android/ios, and for a domain that violates origin policy.

covered.description: True when an active global rule already allows this candidate for every restricted key.

matched_by.description: The global rule that covered the candidate; null when covered is false.

reason.description: Present only when there is something extra to say about a covered=false verdict. This is a verdict code inside a 200 body, not an HTTP error.

AccessTokenIntrospection.description: The token's own identity and scope. Every field below is always present EXCEPT `projects`, which appears only when `all_projects` is false.

can_manage_supabase.description: Whether the token may read the Supabase project vault (separate axis from the project scope; off by default).

can_read_vault.description: Whether the token may read project-vault metadata and presence flags (never a value; off by default).

can_reveal_vault.description: Whether the token may read project-vault credential VALUES, file bytes and .env blocks. Implies can_read_vault; off by default.

can_read_supabase_tokens.description: Whether the token may read a Supabase account's personal access token (sbp_...). A separate axis: can_manage_supabase does NOT grant it, because a PAT reaches every project the account owns. Off by default.

projects.description: The explicit project scope. ABSENT ENTIRELY when all_projects is true — not null, and not an empty array — because an all-projects token covers projects that do not exist yet, so no list could describe it. Test with `'projects' in data`, never `data.projects === null`.

plaintext_key.description: The full key. Shown only by create, rotate and reveal.

ApiKeyWithSecret.description: The key fields flat, plus the plaintext. Create and rotate previously nested this under data.api_key; both are flat as of 2026-07-18.

SupabaseProjectSummary.description: Safe list/summary view of a registered Supabase project. No secret values; `has` flags say which secrets a reveal would return.

ref.description: The `<ref>` label of a `<ref>.supabase.co` URL; null for self-hosted/custom-domain.

account_email.description: The account email to ACT on. Derived from the `account` relation since 2026.08.19.1 — supabase_projects.account_email is a legacy free-text column and the two have disagreed in production, which sends a personal access token lookup to an account that does not own the project (403 on functions deploy while every presence flag reads true).

account.description: Pointer to the Supabase account that owns this project — never its credential. null when the project is not linked to an account.

has_personal_access_token.description: Whether that account has a PAT stored.

credentials_via.description: Path to the account endpoint that can return it.

requires_scope.description: The token scope that endpoint requires.

legacy_account_email_conflict.description: Present and true only when the legacy account_email column still disagrees with this account. The relation wins; `legacy_account_email` carries the stale value for reference.

legacy_account_email.description: The stale free-text value, present only alongside legacy_account_email_conflict.

has.description: Presence flags per secret column, tested WITHOUT decrypting. An empty map encodes as {} (it encoded as [] before 2026.08.19.1).

endpoints.description: Derived from the project URL, not stored. dashboard is null when the URL has no inferable project ref; realtime is derived from the URL host and is null only when the URL has no parseable host.

allOf.description: Detail plus every stored secret and ready-to-paste env blocks. An unreadable secret (e.g. encrypted under a rotated APP_KEY) comes back null.

env.description: Ready-to-paste .env fragments; a block absent when it would be empty.

PaginationMessage.description: A human- and agent-readable restatement of `meta`: position, how much remains, and the exact query string for the next page. Also states when per_page was capped, so a truncated response is never mistaken for missing data.
examples: Showing 1-20 of 137 (page 1 of 7). 117 more available - request page 2 to continue (?page=2&per_page=20).
Showing 121-137 of 137 (page 7 of 7). This is the last page.

help.description: Where in that service's console the value is found.

secret.description: Encrypted at rest and withheld from every non-reveal response.

client_safe.description: May appear in a generated VITE_/NEXT_PUBLIC_ block. Always false when `secret` is true.

env_key.description: Unprefixed .env name, or null when the value never belongs in one.

freeform.description: True for `general`, where you name the keys yourself.

linked.description: Set on `supabase`, which links to the account-wide vault instead of storing its own fields.

derived.description: The service's block is computed by FilesHub, not stored. Added 2026.08.20.1.

writable.description: Whether PUT /projects/{project}/vault/{service} accepts fields for it — false for linked and derived services. Added 2026.08.20.1.

registered.description: False when the registry does not declare this service but the project stores rows under it. Those rows are real and readable, but they carry no field help, no env_key and no client_safe flag, so nothing derived from the registry (the env blocks, client-safe filtering) can include them. Added 2026.08.19.1 — before that such a service had no entry here at all.

has.description: Which fields hold a value. Tested without decrypting, so a value stored under a rotated APP_KEY still reports true. Since 2026.08.19.1 this is the union of the registry's DECLARED fields and every field actually stored — a credential under an undeclared key used to be absent entirely. An empty map encodes as {} (it encoded as [] before that release).

values.description: Non-secret values only, unless this came from a reveal. An UNDECLARED field has no registry entry marking it safe, so it is treated as secret and withheld here. Empty encodes as {}.

derived.description: True when the block is COMPUTED by FilesHub from records it already holds rather than stored. Only `fileshub` today. A derived service refuses writes. Added 2026.08.20.1.

writable.description: False for a linked service (`supabase`) or a derived one (`fileshub`). Added 2026.08.20.1.

shadowed_stored_fields.description: Present on a derived service only: stored rows that exist under it from before it became derived. Named rather than silently overridden. Added 2026.08.20.1.

download.description: Path to fetch the bytes. Present on reveal responses.

app_identifier.description: Reverse-DNS app id. IMMUTABLE once published to a store.

unregistered_services.description: Services this project stores rows under that the registry does not declare — almost always a label typed where a key belongs ("Google Cloud" for "google_cloud"). Named at the top level so a reader never has to diff against GET /vault/services to notice. Each also appears in `services` with registered:false, and is addressable at GET|POST /projects/{project}/vault/{service}. Added to the project detail in 2026.08.19.1 and to EVERY /vault/projects list row in 2026.08.19.2 — the list is the surface a fleet sweep reads, and on 2026-08-19 six of the seven non-empty projects were orphans under a single free-text string.

supabase.description: Pointer to the account-wide Supabase vault, never a copy of its credentials — reading those needs the can_manage_supabase scope. Null when this project has no linked Supabase record.

ref.description: The <ref> label of a <ref>.supabase.co URL; null for a self-hosted or custom-domain project.

credentials_via.description: Path to the endpoint that returns them, e.g. /api/public/v1/supabase-projects/abcdefgh.

ai_accounts.description: AI accounts assigned to this project, as POINTERS — never keys. Added 2026.08.21.1.

env.description: Ready-to-paste .env fragments. `vite` and `next` contain ONLY client_safe values, so a server secret cannot reach a browser bundle by mistake. EVERY KEY IS OPTIONAL: a block that would be empty is dropped rather than returned as "", so a project with nothing configured returns `env: {}`. Handle the missing key — piping an absent block into a file writes an empty file with no error.

undecryptable.description: `service.field` names that HOLD a value which could not be decrypted — stored under a previous APP_KEY. Reported honestly so you can tell 'not set' from 'set but unreadable'. Re-enter those in the dashboard.

SupabaseAccountSummary.description: Safe view of a Supabase account — never the personal access token, only whether one is stored.

has.description: Which credentials this account holds, tested without decrypting.

projects_count.description: Registered Supabase projects a reveal of this account would reach.

dashboard.description: Derived supabase.com pages for this account.

projects.description: Supabase projects registered under this account.

credentials_via.description: That project's own vault endpoint — a different scope (can_manage_supabase).

SupabaseAccountDetail.description: One account with its dashboard pages and the projects underneath it. Still no token value.

personal_access_token.description: The sbp_... token, or null when stored but undecryptable.

env.description: Ready-to-paste .env fragment. Omitted keys mean no value is stored.

cli.description: SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=... — the variable the Supabase CLI reads.

SupabaseAccountReveal.description: Everything, the personal access token included. Recorded on every call.

VaultServiceWrite.description: Partial upsert for one service. 3.1 note: a null in `values` is MEANINGFUL — it deletes that field's row — which is why the value type is a nullable string rather than a plain one.

values.description: Field key -> value. An absent key is left alone; an explicit null DELETES that field's row.

secrets.description: Field key -> whether to treat the value as secret. Honoured ONLY on the freeform `general` service; for a registry-declared field the registry decides and this is ignored, because the non-reveal views filter on exactly that flag. Absent defaults to true (fail closed).

VaultBulkWrite.description: Many services in one transaction. Validated in full before any write.

services.description: Service key -> its values map, same semantics as VaultServiceWrite.values.

secrets.description: Service key -> (field key -> secret). Freeform rows only.

links.description: When present, REPLACES the whole link list. When absent, the list is untouched; an empty array clears it.

confirm.description: Must be true. Clearing a whole service deletes every credential and file under it, so the acknowledgement is explicit — a caller meaning to clear ONE field should use PUT with a null value instead.

from.description: The source service. MAY be a name the registry never declared — that is the purpose of this endpoint.

to.description: The destination service. Must be registry-declared, or the move would merely relocate the orphan.

keys.description: Source key -> destination key. A key with no entry is carried over unchanged and validated against the destination like any other, so a partial map fails loudly rather than leaving rows behind.

VaultFileWrite.description: The JSON form of a config-file upload. The multipart form (a `file` part) is equivalent.

content_base64.description: Base64 of the RAW file bytes — no data: URI prefix. Decoded strictly and size-checked AFTER decoding, so a corrupted payload is refused rather than stored as something that fails at use time.

VaultChanges.description: What the write moved, as FIELD NAMES (`service.key`) only — never a value. The same names are what the audit log records.

ProjectVaultWriteResult.description: Every write answers with the SAME payload GET /projects/{project}/vault returns — so a caller confirms what landed without a second call and without needing can_reveal_vault — plus the changes block.

AiAccountAssignment.description: A POINTER to an AI account — never a credential.

purpose.description: What this project uses the account FOR — chat, embeddings, transcription.

credentials_via.description: The endpoint that would return the key.

note.description: Names the scope that endpoint requires.

via.description: How this project reaches the account. `explicit` is a pivot row somebody wrote; `all_projects` is the account-level standing rule, which can only be undone on the account.

AiAccountSummary.description: An AI account without its key.

console.description: The provider's own key page — derived, not stored.

has.description: Which secret fields hold a value. Tested without decrypting.

all_projects.description: Standing rule: every project may use this account, including projects created later. The `projects` array below stays the EXPLICIT assignments only.

undecryptable.description: Names the field when a value is stored but could not be decrypted (rotated APP_KEY) — distinguishing that from 'not set', which an indistinguishable null would not.

env.description: Only ever a `node` block. 🔴 There is deliberately no vite/next block: an AI key must never reach a browser bundle.

AiAccountWrite.description: Create or update. On update every key is optional; a BLANK api_key is dropped rather than stored.

api_key.description: Blank is IGNORED, so editing another field cannot wipe the credential. Use clear_api_key to remove it.

clear_api_key.description: Update only. The unambiguous way to remove a stored key — a blank value cannot mean this, because ConvertEmptyStringsToNull makes an empty string and null identical to the controller.

all_projects.description: Set true to let every project use this account, now and in future. For a snapshot of today's projects instead, use PUT /ai-accounts/{account}/projects with all_existing.

ProjectAiAccountsWrite.description: A full replace. An empty array unassigns every account.

AiAccountProjectsWrite.description: Send EITHER project_ids OR all_existing — never both. They mean different things and the precedence between them is deliberately undefined, so a body carrying both is refused with 422.

project_ids.description: Replace the explicit assignment set with exactly these projects. An empty array detaches all of them. An id the token cannot reach answers 404.

all_existing.description: A SNAPSHOT: attach every project that exists right now (and that this token may reach). A project created later is NOT covered — for that, set all_projects on the account itself.
